author: TIM SEAMAN
title: Finalists for Sioux City Police Chief meet with public - NewsBreak
text:
By TIM SEAMAN Maren Ewertz ,
1 days ago
SIOUX CITY , Iowa ( KCAU ) — Wednesday night was the meet-and-greet for the two candidates vying for Sioux City Police Chief.
Robert Trebes has more than two decades of experience in municipal policing for the Bullhead Police Department, becoming Chief there in 2021. Likewise, Scott Ebner has more than 30 years of experience in local and state policing, including as Public Safety Director and Chief of Police for Glynn County, Georgia.
KCAU 9 asked both what led them to the Sioux City opening.
“The population of Glenn County is around 90,000 people; the size of the police department is authorized at 132, just like here,” said Ebner. “There’s just over 900 county employees, just like there are city employees here, and it’s an area I truly like.”
“So I wanted to look for an area that seemed to be in line with my values that I was raised with,” said Trebes. “Really, in a nutshell kind of felt like this is a good fit for me; hopefully they feel the same way.”
Story continues below
Flock cameras, or better described as license plate reading cameras, have drawn a lot of attention in the Sioux City area. At last check, Sioux City has a dozen Flock cameras in use; South Sioux City has more than 30.
“But it has to be monitored, it has to be regulated, and officers need to be trained,” said Ebner. “I went so far as I put more standards in place.”
“I worry about making sure the proper safeguards are in place,” said Trebes. “To make sure that people’s constitutional rights are upheld, that privacy is not embedded more than it needs to be for the government’s needs in order to investigate crimes.”
City Manager Mike Collett said 19 people, including one from the Sioux City Department, officially applied for the job. Four finalists emerged from testing, with only Trebes and Ebner choosing to move forward in the process.
Whoever is hired will take over for Rex Mueller, who is retiring after nine years as Chief and 30 years in the Sioux City Police Department.
